blocks.html:
Nobody uses a tool until they have been trained and signed off on it. These rules apply every time you enter the shop:

  • Safety glasses on at all times, even if you are only watching.
  • Closed-toe shoes, no loose clothing or jewelry, and long hair tied back.
  • Never work alone. A trained member or mentor must be present.
  • Know where the first aid kit, fire extinguisher and emergency stop are.
  • Clean up your station before you leave.

Training goes in three steps for every machine:

  1. Watch: a trained member demonstrates the tool and its hazards.
  2. Practice: you make a test part while they supervise.
  3. Sign-off: a lead or mentor confirms you can use it on your own.

Start with hand tools, then the drill press and band saw, before moving to larger machines.

• Most structure uses #10-32 and 1/4-20 bolts with nylon-insert lock nuts.
  • Use rivets for gussets and sheet metal that never needs to come apart.
  • Use blue thread-locker on bolts that go into tapped holes and could vibrate loose.
  • Always deburr cut edges and drilled holes before assembly.

1. Get the drawing (or DXF/toolpath) from CAD and check it is the latest revision.
  2. Mark and cut stock, then machine features in order.
  3. Deburr and check every critical dimension against the drawing.
  4. Label the part and log it as done so assembly knows it is ready.
